title: Stability Ledger — Two-Week Onboarding & Regression Insights (2026-06-16)
summary: Two-week snapshot focusing on onboarding regressions observed across three recently onboarded model families. Purpose: capture trajectory of quality metrics, cluster failure archetypes, and surface low-effort mitigations we can push before the next canary. This doc mixes telemetry, short manual triage notes, and a prioritized action list for eng + applied ML.
highlights: Aggregate quality index (Q-index) down 4.7 points on convo-style promptsets since 2026-06-01; most degradation concentrated in turn-level factuality and persona-anchoring prompts.

Three dominant failure archetypes identified: hallucinated facts with high confidence, prompt-compaction drop (loss of instruction fidelity when prompts shortened), and tokenization boundary errors for multilingual Spanish-Portuguese hybrid inputs.
Quick win implemented: gated fallback to v1-quantized for high-latency tails reduced error-rate for one customer suite by 21% — anecdotal but repeatable in replay tests.
Open question: whether the recent scheduler kernel update altered prefix-kv retention behavior for long-context chat workloads — logs show increased cache evictions coincident with regression window.
top_failures: Archetype A — Confident Hallucination: prompts that ask for short factual lists ("top 5 CEOs of X industry" style) now return fabricated entries with high-probability tokens. Example: prompt-id ps-294 produced 'J. Harrow' (fabricated) with p>0.9. Observed after model->quantized recompile on 2026-06-03.

Archetype B — Instruction Loss with Compaction: when client-side prompt shorteners trim system instructions, model drifts from safety constraints and outputs unsafe or off-brand phrasing. Reproducible with compacted promptset 'compact-chat-47'.

Archetype C — Tokenization Boundary Noise: mixed Spanish/Portuguese inputs near tokenizer boundaries result in doubled diacritics and truncated entities (e.g., 'São Paulo' -> 'Sãõ Paulo'). Correlated with new token-merging table in tokenizer-v2 rollout.
